headline: South Asia: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated’ airstrikes against terrorist targets in border region with Afghanistan
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated’ airstrikes against terrorist targets in border region with Afghanistan.
- India: Trump dodged Yemen's plea for military support amid Houthi attacks on Riyadh: Report.
- Persian Gulf Region: Trump calls off planned US strikes on Houthis at last minute after Saudi plea - report.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
- Military Times, South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Poll: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as war continues.
Only 34% of respondents in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll said they approved of the strikes on Iran.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Airmen can’t get enough of new, warlike basic training, leaders say.
Six months after the Air Force launched a tougher, more combat-centric training program, airmen and prospective instructors are clamoring to get involved.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Robinson hits back at recovery claims - Opposition finance spokesman warns of more pain ahead.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Robinson hits back at recovery claims - Opposition finance spokesman warns of more pain ahead.
Opposition Spokesman on Finance Julian Robinson is warning that there is trouble ahead for Jamaican households, countering reports that the country’s economy is recovering faster than projected. Robinson said the economy has contracted for the last three quarters and is projected to contract again for a fourth quarter. Addressing party supporters at the People’s National Party’s (PNP) 88th Annual Conference in Westmoreland on Sunday, he pointed to a near-eight per cent inflation rate, and a $28.7-billion revenue shortfall that forced $30 billion in new borrowing.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentine bookshops declare ‘bookselling emergency’.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 6 hours ago: Argentine bookshops declare ‘bookselling emergency’.
The country’s bookshops federation and the Buenos Aires book fair organizers warned that a sharp drop in book sales and rising costs are threatening independent stores La entrada Argentine bookshops declare ‘bookselling emergency’ se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

- The Moscow Times, 7 hours ago: As Fears of Post-Election Mobilization Swirl, Russian Activists Prepare for the Worst.
Anti-war activists and lawyers say that anxiety is rising, even though helping Russians avoid military service has long been a routine part of their work.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Satellite images show damage to Shahed storage bunkers at Russian drone base.
New satellite images show damaged bunkers, warehouses and a launch area at Russia’s Tsymbulovo drone base after a 21 September strike, with burnt-out UAVs visible at the site.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Man killed in Russian drone strike on residential building in Sloviansk – photos.
Rescue workers recovered the body of a man trapped under rubble after a Russian drone hit a five-storey building in Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Zelenskyy responds to Trump and says Ukraine is ready for de-escalation: "Solutions are possible".
Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for reciprocal de-escalation if Russia stops strikes on energy, critical infrastructure and food exports.

- Balkan Insight, 7 hours ago: UN Chief Condemns Mladic Glorification in Meeting with Bosnian Leader.
At a meeting at UN headquarters with chair of Bosnia and Herzegovina's presidency, secretary-general Antonio Guterres says glorification of war criminals is a threat to regional reconciliation and stability.

AFRICA

IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi tells Fars News Agency that Iran is ready to change the 'weaponry and geography of the war.'
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 8 hours ago: Poor storage or sabotage? Series of explosions in Syria raises fears.
Repeated blasts at military sites expose the risks facing Syria as it rebuilds its army after years of war.
- Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: One police officer wounded in shooting attack near Ontario synagogue on Yom Kippur.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford also condemned the shooting in a post on social media, saying Jewish community members had "every right to gather and worship safely and without fear."

- Africanews, 15 hours ago: Iran says large numbers of army ground forces remain deployed along borders.
Iran has kept large numbers of army ground forces deployed along its borders since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 in response to potential threats, the commander of the army's ground forces said on Sunday.
- Africanews, 6 hours ago: Cameroon: Thousands flee the Far North after Boko Haram attack [Africanews Today].
In Cameroon, insecurity is triggering a fresh wave of displacement in the Far North. Following an attack attributed to Boko Haram that left 15 people dead, thousands of residents are fleeing towards border towns, raising fears of another humanitarian crisis

[ENA] Addis Ababa -- Sudan's warring parties should acknowledge that neither can secure an outright military victory and give negotiations a chance to end the conflict, Getachew Reda, adviser to the Ethiopian Prime Minister on East African affairs, said.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Somalia: Somalia Says Intelligence Operation Kills Four Al-Shabab Members in Middle Shabelle.
[Shabelle] Mogadishu, Somalia -- Somalia's National Intelligence and Security Agency, with support from international partners, killed four members of the al-Shabab militant group and wounded another in planned operations in Middle Shabelle region, the agency said.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: Namibia: Father, Son Killed in Hippo Attack.
[New Era] Ikaba -- A father and his son drowned after a hippopotamus reportedly attacked and overturned their canoe while a family of five was crossing a channel near Ikaba in the Zambezi region on Friday.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Malawi: Malawi's Climate Fight 'Strangled' By Crushing Debt Burden, Actionaid Warns.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi is being denied the chance to fight back against climate change because a staggering 24 percent of the national budget is being swallowed up by debt repayments, campaigners have warned.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 11 hours ago: South Africa: SAWS Warns of Rainfall and Thundershowers.
[SAnews.gov.za] The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has forecast that a surface high-pressure system will extend its ridge into the eastern and southern parts of the country this week, bringing isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: Rotary Club Rallies Malawians to Donate Blood for Children Battling Cancer.
[Nyasa Times] A Lilongwe charity has launched an urgent blood donation drive to support children undergoing cancer treatment, as Malawi marks Childhood Cancer Awareness Month this September -- with organisers revealing hundreds of children are diagnosed with the disease in the country every single year.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated’ airstrikes against terrorist targets in border region with Afghanistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated’ airstrikes against terrorist targets in border region with Afghanistan.
Pakistan conducted airstrikes on terrorist sites “in the border region with Afghanistan”, killing more than 28 terrorists, the information ministry said on Monday. In a statement, the ministry stressed that the “calibrated” strikes were carried out “against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations responsible” for the recent multiple terrorist incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Oil prices slide on hopes of diplomacy in Iran war.
Oil prices slid to their ​lowest in more than a week on Monday as investors hoped for diplomatic progress on the US-Israeli war on Iran due to this ‌week’s UN meeting and eyed a partial recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. Brent crude futures and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude touched their lowest since September 10 earlier on Monday. The Brent contract for November was at $102.09 a barrel at 11:55am PKT, down $1.78, or 1.71 per cent, ​after settling 0.91pc lower on Friday.
- The Hindu - International, 14 hours ago: Pakistan strikes militant hideouts in Afghanistan, killing 28; Kabul disputes toll.
The Taliban said a house in Kunar province was hit, killing three members of one family, days after an attack on a police facility in Pakistan
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Naqvi meets Iranian counterpart, president; Tehran lauds Pakistan's efforts for regional peace.
Tehran on Monday thanked Pakistan’s military and civilian leadership for its efforts for regional peace and stability as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with his Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni in Tehran. Later, he also held a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, according to Iran’s state-run Press TV. According to Pakistan’s interior ministry, Naqvi and Momeni exchanged views on “Pakistan-Iran bilateral relations and the latest situation in the region”.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Trump dodged Yemen's plea for military support amid Houthi attacks on Riyadh: Report.
President Trump did not commit US forces to aid Yemen against the Houthis. Yemeni President Alimi sought American backing for his government's efforts. US officials met Houthi representatives in Oman, discussing a ceasefire. Trump reportedly called off planned airstrikes against Houthi targets. The conflict has caused significant casualties and displacement within Yemen.

Retiring deputy police commissioner Andrew Kan Kai-yan has said artificial intelligence (AI) poses a new threat to national security in Hong Kong, with the force turning to the emerging technology to help combat the issue. Kan raised the alarm after state security minister Chen Yixin warned last week of rising national security risks posed by AI.
